judgeNotes.zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: The build-up proceeds by flat rectangular colour slabs and a large dark mass dropped in region-by-region with texture sharpening only at the end, reading as a digital mosaic/wipe progression rather than a brush-and-pen painting order.
judgeNotes.Qwen/Qwen3.5-9B: The sequence depicts a digital posterization or low-resolution fill effect using rectangular blocks, rather than brushwork or ink wash.

hills.painterNote: Trees go from olive stamped crowns to blue-slate masses (sage-slate wet underwash, masked lit crown tops, one connected navy shadow glaze across the woods), grass gets a brighter lime base plus a green second wash with yellow patches left, and ink gets stronger (trail edges, trunks, branches), because a1 was olive, stamp-like and too yellow-pale in the grass compared with the target.

judgeNotes.zai-org/GLM-5.3-Flash: A believable watercolor build-up — pale first tint, wet-edged hull block-in, then darks and finally rigging and chain details — with only the slightly even blue hull slab at 25% as a minor tell.

sargent.painterNote: Invert the value structure to match the target: the hull becomes one connected mid-blue wash (charged darker wet-in-wet at its turns, paler upper-middle) against a pale cream background, and the polygon sweeps and blocky darks become feathered curved strokes, because attempt 1's pale hull on a blue background lost the bow's form and read as stripes and slabs.
